issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 4 suffers from multiple severe mathematical defects: (1) The left-hand side evaluates the gradient at an averaged iterate \bar{\theta}_K inside a minimum over k, but \bar{\theta}_K is undefined in the theorem, does not depend on the running index k, and for general smooth nonconvex functions SGD does not guarantee that the gradient norm at an averaged iterate \bar{\theta}_K converges to zero. (2) The parameter L_f appearing in the step size and in the bound is undefined anywhere in the paper (Assumption 1 only defines individual smoothness constants L_i and L_{\max}). (3) The bound depends on \Delta_f^* := \inf f - \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m \inf f_i, which requires each component f_i to be bounded below; however, neither Assumption 1 nor Assumption 3 requires f_i to be bounded below, so \inf f_i can be -\infty, rendering \Delta_f^* undefined or +\infty. (4) The theorem invokes Assumption 3 (bounded variance \sigma^2), but neither the step size nor the convergence bound depends on \sigma^2, conflating incompatible convergence analyses from the literature.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Theorem 4 with a valid nonconvex SGD convergence theorem: change the guarantee type to the minimum iterate norm \min_{0 \le k \le K-1} \mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(\theta_k)\|^2] (or a randomly sampled iterate), define L_f as the smoothness constant of f, explicitly assume each f_i is bounded below (or replace the bound with the standard bounded-variance nonconvex SGD bound depending on \sigma^2), and eliminate the undefined \bar{\theta}_K.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4 is mathematically invalid and non-executable: the step size cannot be determined due to undefined L_f, the bound is vacuous or undefined if component functions are unbounded below, and the asserted convergence of the gradient at the averaged iterate \bar{\theta}_K does not hold for nonconvex functions.
issues.title: Invalid stationarity guarantee, missing hypotheses, and undefined parameters in nonconvex SGD theorem
issues.why_classification: No valid version of the claimed guarantee on \bar{\theta}_K survives in the nonconvex regime without changing the central guarantee type, introducing missing lower-bound assumptions and undefined parameters, and the source provides no proof to support a resolution.
